rules.title: Prohibition on Algorithmic Devices for Rent Setting
rules.requirement: The sale or use of algorithmic devices to set rents or manage occupancy levels for residential units in San Francisco is prohibited. An algorithmic device is defined as a device such as a software program that uses algorithms to analyze nonpublic competitor rental data for the purposes of providing a landlord recommendations on what rent to charge for a vacant unit.
rules.quoted_span: The law prohibits the sale or use of algorithmic devices to set rents or manage occupancy levels for residential units in San Francisco.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to residential units in San Francisco; applies to any entity selling or using algorithmic devices
rules.sanctions: Civil action may be brought by a tenant or the City Attorney for violation

field_evidence.quoted_span: The law prohibits the sale or use of algorithmic devices to set rents or manage occupancy levels for residential units in San Francisco.

Legislation
adding Section 37.10C to the Rent Ordinance went into effect on October 14, 2024.
allows a tenant or the City Attorney to bring a civil action if they believe an entity is in violation of the law
